Class String

  • java.lang.Object
    • java.lang.String
  • All implemented interfaces
    Serializable ， CharSequence ， Comparable<String> 
    public final class String
extends Object
implements Serializable, Comparable<String>, CharSequence
    StringThe class represents strings. All string literals in Java programs (e.g."abc") are all implemented as instances of this class.

    Strings are immutable; Their values cannot be changed after they are created. String buffers support mutable strings. Because String objects are immutable, they can be shared. For example: 

         String str = "abc";

    Equivalent to: 

         char data[] = {'a', 'b', 'c'};
     String str = new String(data);

    Here are some examples of how to use strings: 

         System.out.println("abc");
     String cde = "cde";
     System.out.println("abc" + cde);
     String c = "abc".substring(2,3);
     String d = cde.substring(1, 2);

    The Java language provides special support for the string concatenation operator (+), and for conversion of other objects to strings. For further information on string concatenation and conversion, seeJava Language Specification 。

      • split

        public String[] split​(String regex,
                      int limit)
        Splits this string around the givenof a regular expressionmatchitem 。

        The array returned by this method contains each substring of this string that is terminated by another substring matching the given expression, or by the end of the string. The substrings in the array are arranged in the order in which they appear in this string. If the expression does not match any part of the input, then the resulting array has just one element, namely that string.

        When there is a positive-width match at the beginning of the string, an empty leading substring is included at the beginning of the resulting array. However, a zero-width match at the beginning never produces such an empty leading substring.

        limitThe parameter controls the number of times the pattern is applied and therefore affects the length of the resulting array.

        • ifLimitis positive, the pattern will be applied at mostLimit- 1 times, the length of the array will not exceedLimit, and the last entry of the array will contain all input beyond the last matched delimiter.

        • ifLimitIf it is zero, the pattern will be applied as many times as possible, the array can have any length, and trailing empty strings will be discarded.

        • ifLimitIf negative, then the pattern will be applied as many times as possible, and the array can have any length.

        For example, the string"boo:and:foo"Using the following parameters produces the following results:

        Split example showing regex, limit, and result
        Regex Limit Result
        : 2 { "boo", "and:foo" }
        5 { "boo", "and", "foo" }
        -2 { "boo", "and", "foo" }
        o 5 { "b", "", ":and:f", "", "" }
        -2 { "b", "", ":and:f", "", "" }
        0 { "b", "", ":and:f" }

        Callstrthis method of the form。 split( regex , n )produces the same result as the expression

        Pattern.compile(regex).split(str, n)
        Parameter
        regexThe delimiting regular expression
        limit- result threshold, as described above
        Result
        an array of strings computed by splitting this string around matches of the given regular expression
        Exception
        PatternSyntaxExceptionIf the syntax of the regular expression is invalid
        Starting from the following version:
        1.4
        See also:
        Pattern

      • toLowerCase

        public String toLowerCase()
        Using the rules of the default locale, thisStringAll characters are converted to lowercase. This is equivalent to callingtoLowerCase(Locale.getDefault()) 。

        Note:This method is locale-sensitive, and if used with strings intended to be interpreted independently of the locale, it may produce unexpected results. Examples are programming language identifiers, protocol keys, and HTML tags. For example,"TITLE".toLowerCase()In the Turkish locale, returns"t\u0131tle", where 'ı' is the Latin small letter dotless i character. To obtain correct results for locale-insensitive strings, usetoLowerCase(Locale.ROOT) 。

        Result
        String, converted to lowercase.
        See also:
        toLowerCase(Locale)

      • lines

        public Stream<String> lines()
        Returns a stream of lines extracted from this string, separated by line terminators.

        line terminatoris one of the following: a line feed"\n"(U + 000A), carriage return character"\r"(U+000D), or a carriage return line feed immediately followed by"\r\n" （U + 000D U + 000A） 。

        One lineis a sequence of zero or more characters followed by a line terminator, or a sequence of one or more characters followed by the end of the string. A line does not include a line terminator.

        The stream returned by this method contains the lines appearing in this string.

        API Note:
        ThisOf the lineThe definition implies that an empty string has zero lines, and that there is no empty line after a line terminator at the end of the string.
        Implementation Note:
        By lazily providing elements and searching for new line terminators more quickly, this method provides better performance than split("\R").
        Result
        A stream of lines extracted from this string
        Starting from the following version:
        11
